CpG ODN, a Toll-like receptor 7/8 ligand and alpha-galactosyleramide, a NKT cell agonist, both induced the activation of a number of pathways and genes in the mouse vagina, which were involved in immune response, inflammation, cell death, cell cycle, and DNA repair.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Toll-like receptor 5 and 9 agonists and the invariant natural-killer T-cell agonist alpha-galatcosylceramide share a common set of molecular pathways in the mouse vaginal epithelium that are involved in immune activation and inflammation, and these pathways are distinct from the pathways that are involved in the vaginal epithelial response to estrogen and progesterone.
